title: Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced
provenance: tested locally on Apple Silicon (M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r4) on 2026-09-08: it launches and loads under vkd3d and the GPU device is then lost, twice, at default and at minimum settings
notes: Starts but does not stay up on the engines Highball ships today, and the reason is now measured. The game needs Highball's Wine 11 engine (CrossOver 26.3 base) and two graphics modes in one process tree: the Rockstar Games Launcher signs in under DXMT, the game is DirectX 12 only. Under D3DMetal the game creates a device and then quits with ERR_GFX_D3D_NOD3D12, because it requires DirectX 12 Enhanced Barriers (it declares Agility SDK version 611) and D3DMetal 3.0 reports EnhancedBarriersSupported = 0. vkd3d reports 1, and under vkd3d the game reaches the story-mode loading screen at 53-62 fps, then loses the GPU device because MoltenVK cannot translate some of its shaders to Metal. So neither path is complete: D3DMetal has the shaders but not the barriers, vkd3d has the barriers but not the shaders. CrossOver's 2026 preview, which carries a newer D3DMetal, is reported to run the game well on Apple Silicon, so the D3DMetal side is the one that closes. Turn BattlEye off in the launcher first (Settings > My installed games), its driver cannot load under Wine. GTA Online is out of reach regardless. If sign-in is refused with #1.000.7, set the Mac's clock (see the rockstar recipe).

requiresLauncher.name: Rockstar Games Launcher
requiresLauncher.note: Required for sign-in. Works on the Wine 11 engine under DXMT with the cross-process browser fix; sign-in verified 2026-09-08 once the Mac's clock was right. The game must then run under vkd3d while the launcher stays on DXMT.

anticheat.note: GTA Online only; BattlEye's Linux/Proton support does not extend to macOS.

knownIssues.symptom: ERR_GFX_D3D_NOD3D12 the moment the game starts, under the D3DMetal graphics mode
knownIssues.cause: measured 2026-09-08 on an M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r4: the game creates a D3D12 device successfully and then refuses. D3DMetal 3.0 reports EnhancedBarriersSupported = 0 in D3D12_FEATURE_D3D12_OPTIONS12, and GTA5_Enhanced.exe declares Agility SDK version 611, whose barrier API the game uses. It also reports RaytracingTier 0, RelaxedFormatCastingSupported 0 and CopyQueueTimestampQueriesSupported 0 where vkd3d reports 1, 1 and 1. This is not the Agility SDK loader: the game never calls D3D12GetInterface, it loads d3d12.dll and calls D3D12CreateDevice directly. It also explains why the game ran on D3DMetal before Rockstar's 2025 patch and not after.
knownIssues.fix: none at the app level. It needs a D3DMetal with Enhanced Barriers; Highball ships a fixed engine as soon as one exists.

knownIssues.symptom: Under vkd3d it loads to a black screen with only the progress bar, then exits on its own near the end of the load
knownIssues.cause: MoltenVK cannot translate some of the game's shaders to Metal, so vkd3d gets no pipeline for them: 27 compute and 42 graphics pipelines refused ('reinterpret_cast casts away qualifiers', 'indirection requires pointer operand', 'automatic variable qualified with an address space'). The loading screen art is among them, which is why the background stays black while the bar still moves. The run ends in VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, Metal failing a command buffer with 'Invalid Resource (code 9)', exit 5. Reproduced twice, at default settings and with every setting at minimum, same stage, so it is not a quality setting or a memory ceiling.
knownIssues.fix: none at the app level; it needs MoltenVK to translate those shaders. Stock MoltenVK 1.4.2 in place of the engine's build does not start at all, the engine's vkd3d expects its own fork.
